subject: [PATCH for-7.5 4/5] memcg: avoid queuing high_work from reclaim

2026-10-10.patch_summary: This patch prevents the high_work worker from queuing itself during memory reclamation by skipping memory.high enforcement for tasks that would use high_work and have PF_MEMALLOC set, thus avoiding infinite recursion.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: reviewer suggested unifying the high_work check with an existing main charging path check
reviews.raw_body:
The patch itself looks OK. I am wondering whether we can unify the check
with the existing one which forces the allocation through in main
charging path.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged a potential issue where high_work worker could queue itself indefinitely, but clarified that the patch does not delay actual charge requests.

Author addressed Michal Hocko's concern that moving the check for PF_MEMALLOC into try_charge_memcg would not prevent high_work from queuing itself, explaining that successful charges bypass memory.high enforcement and proposing to move the check directly into the high enforcement function.
reviews.raw_body:
It will not delay the actual charge request. This mainly means that we keep
enqueing the high reclaim work even from high reclaim context and can
potentially keep wasting CPU if high reclaim is not very successful.

---

The force charge (and ENOMEM) paths bypass the memory.high enforcement
altogether. Only successful charges (done_restock label) goes through
memory.high enforcement. So, even if we move this check in try_charge_memcg, it
will still be a separate check before calling high enforcement function. I think
this check is very high_work specific and better to be in the high enforcement
function.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Michal Hocko questioned the necessity of the patch, asking for a clarification on what 'wasting CPU' means and whether there's a practical problem if high_work queues itself from reclaim

Reviewer Michal Hocko suggested a different approach to prevent unbounded recursion when reclaim operations need to allocate memory, by adding a check for PF_MEMALLOC in the try_charge_memcg function and skipping the high_work worker queueing if this condition is met.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the issue is related to high_work kworker queuing itself when there's no reclaimable memory, and explained that this behavior is expected in such scenarios.

Author acknowledges that the reviewer's feedback is valid and suggests either sending a new patch or modifying the existing series to address the issue.
reviews.raw_body:
More specifically if high_work kworker keeps enqueing high_work, most probably
the memcg does not have reclaimable memory and keep retrying it wastes CPU.

---

Oh ok this makes sense. Do you want to send a patch or should I add this in this
series replacing the 4th patch?

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Michal Hocko questioned the specificity of the patch's logic, suggesting that it may not be limited to PF_MEMALLOC contexts as implied by the code

reviewer expressed willingness to let the patch be taken, but didn't attempt compilation and provided no specific feedback or suggestions
reviews.raw_body:
Yes but this is not specific to PF_MEMALLOC context, or do I miss
something?

---

Feel free to take it. I haven't even tried to compile this. Just wanted
to show what I have in mind.

-- 
Michal Hocko
SUSE Labs
